title: Strip dangerous caps from gsr-kms-server and btop
head: a1004b2833d5
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Neither new ALPM hook is included in either runtime PKGBUILD
leads.consequence: On a new installation both helpers are installed, but neither hook is installed under /usr/share/libalpm/hooks; fresh-user migration markers are seeded complete, so installed btop/gsr capabilities remain and package upgrades do not trigger either strip. Add BOTH named hooks to both PKGBUILDs, with their Exec targets in the same package.

leads.summary: Migrated /etc hooks stay unowned and mask replacement package hooks
leads.consequence: Existing users acquire same-named hooks in /etc, without Depends = omarchy. A later packaged fix in /usr/share/libalpm/hooks is shadowed, and removing Omarchy leaves Exec commands referring to removed binaries on subsequent btop/gsr upgrades. `-f` checks preserve any existing file indefinitely, so this does not converge on the future package source. Make ownership/removal and precedence explicit, or avoid permanent copies in /etc.

leads.summary: Normal recording loses freeform region selection, and fullscreen becomes portal-selected
leads.consequence: Once caps are stripped, the menu and CLI recordings route to `-w portal` instead of `select_capture_target`. The portal offers monitor/window/virtual, not a drag-to-select region; `--fullscreen` no longer skips the chooser or guarantees the focused monitor. The manual promises the slurp drag picker, and callers expecting noninteractive fullscreen change behavior. Keep region selection available or explicitly document the mode change and its limits.

leads.summary: Failed or missing setcap reports successful stripping
leads.consequence: A failed setcap returns helper exit 0 (`|| true`), and an absent setcap also takes a successful no-op branch. On an install/upgrade where writing file capabilities fails, the hooks appear successful while dangerous capabilities remain. There is no retry until a subsequent triggering transaction. Check the capability after the operation and propagate failures or diagnose them explicitly.
leads.triage: dropped: `|| true` swallows setcap failure; factual but low value, unchanged since earlier review

leads.summary: Recorder tests textual cap presence, but gsr tests the permitted flag
leads.consequence: If a user restores only the inheritable bit (`cap_sys_admin=i`, permitted bit clear), getcap includes cap_sys_admin and this guard chooses KMS. gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.3 reads CAP_PERMITTED, treats it as missing and invokes pkexec, defeating the asserted portal fallback. Parse the actual permitted flag rather than a substring. Standard Arch-installed `=ep` does not exercise the bug.
leads.triage: dropped: inheritable-only cap edge case outside the cap sets Arch/upstream apply

leads.summary: btop cap reset drops CAP_PERFMON as well as CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH
leads.consequence: Arch btop installs both capabilities. Removing both can make its Intel RAPL package power reading inaccessible and Intel i915/xe GPU perf metrics unavailable on systems that require CAP_PERFMON. If only DAC_READ_SEARCH is targeted, preserve permitted/perfmon instead of `-r`, or document the lost metrics. Whether individual devices still expose metrics depends on their permissions and perf settings.

leads.summary: Portal window capture can exclude the webcam overlay
leads.consequence: With stripped caps, the default portal chooser can capture a window rather than the entire display. The webcam remains a separate pinned `WebcamOverlay` window, and the region anchor is only written for `region:*`, never `portal`; resize uses the overlay's own monitor instead of the portal-selected window. Choosing a window, or another monitor, can leave the webcam outside the captured source despite the webcam menu option and documentation. Ensure camera compositing for portal selections or limit/communicate its supported capture targets.
leads.triage: dropped: portal window capture excluding overlay is a hypothesis; partly within F3

leads.summary: Changed comment asserts portal covers HDR, but shipped gsr forces SDR
leads.consequence: The newly reworded guidance says portal covers HDR. gsr 6.1.3 explicitly warns that portal cannot capture HDR and converts requested HDR codecs to SDR. Users cannot rely on this backend choice to preserve HDR content. Remove/qualify the claim; it was also in the preexisting header, so this is a reasserted, not newly introduced, upstream mismatch.
leads.triage: verified factually (gsr main.c tonemaps HDR to SDR on portal; PR comment says 'Portal covers HDR'); not published, minor and restates a base comment

leads.summary: Package-ownership fixture excludes both new hooks
leads.consequence: `alpm_hooks` names only the three older hooks; two appended checks validate source files and Exec strings, not PKGBUILD installation. Consequently config-test passes while both hooks are omitted from package payload (confirmed on head and merged-tip runs). Add 90-omarchy-strip-btop-caps.hook and 90-omarchy-strip-gsr-kms-caps.hook to `alpm_hooks` and the matching PKGBUILDs.

leads.summary: New capability tests accept a broken implementation
leads.consequence: The tests grep filenames and strings, not the helper outcome, the cap flag semantics, or recorder arguments. A recorder that always runs KMS while retaining those literals, or a strip helper that leaves setcap behind a never-true guard, passes all newly added assertions. Add stubbed positive/negative cap and failed-setcap cases plus an assertion on actual `-w` argument, and test package ownership via the alpm_hooks fixture.

leads.summary: Open PR #7188 collides with this PR's fullscreen portal branch
leads.consequence: #7188 is not stacked and independently reorders the exact `--fullscreen` versus `USE_PORTAL` branch. A three-way merge using the real common ancestor leaves conflict markers in the executable, so those two open PRs need an intentional combined hunk/rebase before both land. The intended portal=true result is already included here, not two independent behavior fixes.

leads.summary: Reinstall-configs can mark security migrations done on an unstripped existing system
leads.consequence: The runtime PKGBUILDs seed /etc/skel/.local/state/omarchy/migrations with every shipped filename. Reinstall-configs overlays /etc/skel/. onto an existing user's home, which includes these markers. If used after installing the PR but before these migrations actually run, omarchy-migrate skips both forever for this user. An omarchy-only upgrade does not trigger btop/gpu-screen-recorder hooks, even if they are later packaged; dangerous caps can persist. Prevent migration marker resync for existing users or independently perform this machine-wide strip at package time.
leads.triage: verified factually (reinstall-configs copies /etc/skel migration markers); general pre-existing mechanism, not published

leads.summary: A declined portal request can leave a webcam overlay running while the recorder claims success
leads.consequence: The newly default portal path can return a nonzero cancel/error response before creating a recording. The wrapper waits for the recorder to die, has no failure branch if no output file appears, and returns success; its `start_screenrecording || cleanup_webcam` caller therefore does not close the separately started webcam overlay. The user sees no recorded MP4 or failure notification and, with webcam enabled, a stranded camera window. Handle the dead-before-output branch, distinguish a canceled chooser if desired, and clean up any webcam overlay; related open #7189 addresses a notification but not this cleanup.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up-1 confirmed with source + stubbed run; published as N1

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12103#issuecomment-5856312293), checked at head `a1004b28`. The three new commits resolve the style-test failure. The other earlier findings are unchanged by those commits and still apply. One suggestion in the `/etc` hook finding needs a correction, and one new issue is noted below.

| Earlier finding | Status at `a1004b28` |
|---|---|
| `bin-style-test.sh` fails on raw `command -v` | Resolved |
| Hooks not packaged, fresh installs keep both capabilities | Still present |
| Portal becomes the default, `--fullscreen` becomes interactive | Still present |
| Migration `/etc/pacman.d/hooks` copies | Still present; suggested change corrected below |
| btop loses CPU package power and Intel GPU monitoring | Still present |
| Optional test improvement (string-only tests) | Still applies |

**Verified:** `test/shell.d/bin-style-test.sh` now passes at the head and at the head merged with the current `quattro` tip (exit 0), and still fails at the earlier head (exit 1, listing the same three files). `omarchy-cmd-present getcap`/`setcap` behaved identically to the replaced `command -v … >/dev/null 2>&1` checks in all 29 stubbed scenarios with the helper on `PATH`, with both the base and the current `quattro` version of the helper: same exit status, same `setcap` calls, no output. No regression from the new commits was found.

**Optional:** a simpler option also exists. `AGENTS.md` says commands from the default package set are runtime invariants to be invoked directly, without `omarchy-cmd-present` checks. `setcap` and `getcap` come from libcap, which coreutils depends on, so the three checks could be dropped entirely.

### Hook packaging (reply to the author's comment)

The reply calls hook packaging a separate omarchy-pkgs follow-up. No companion omarchy-pkgs PR or branch was found. At omarchy-pkgs `a701a8db`, both the `omarchy` and `omarchy-dev` PKGBUILDs still install three hooks by name. In this repository, `alpm_hooks` in `config-test.sh` still lists three. The PR description's test-plan item "Fresh install / upgrade runs both strip migrations and pacman hooks" therefore still does not hold for fresh installs. The omarchy PKGBUILD also seeds migration markers into `/etc/skel`, so users created later skip the strip migrations too.

`docs/file-layout.md` shows `default/libalpm/hooks/*.hook` mapping to `/usr/share/libalpm/hooks/*.hook` as a glob, which the PKGBUILDs do not do. That may explain the expectation, but each hook still needs its own install line. Other contributors have opened such companion PRs directly (for example omarchy-pkgs #381 and #645).

**Impact:** as in the earlier review, fresh installs keep `cap_sys_admin=ep` on `gsr-kms-server` and `cap_dac_read_search,cap_perfmon=ep` on btop, because neither the new hooks nor the strip migrations run there.

**Suggested change:** open the omarchy-pkgs PR that adds both hooks to the `omarchy` and `omarchy-dev` PKGBUILDs and link it here, and add both names to `alpm_hooks` in `config-test.sh` in this PR; or mark the fresh-install test-plan item as not covered.

### Correction: `Depends = omarchy` does not silence an orphaned `/etc` hook

The earlier review suggested adding `Depends = omarchy` if the migrations keep writing `/etc/pacman.d/hooks` copies. That does not fix the orphan case. In pacman 7.1.0 (`lib/libalpm/hook.c`), an unsatisfied `Depends` logs `unable to run hook …: could not satisfy dependencies`, so after `omarchy` is removed the error message changes but the error remains. The rest of that finding (a same-named `/etc` hook overrides the packaged one and is never updated, the migration replaces a `/dev/null` mask, and re-stripping on upgrade undoes `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_USE_KMS` after a restore) is unchanged.

**Suggested change:** once the hooks are packaged, have the migrations strip the capability without writing `/etc` copies.

### New: cancelling the portal share dialog leaves the webcam overlay running

With the capability stripped, every recording, including `--fullscreen`, now opens the portal share dialog unless `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_USE_KMS=true` is set. When that dialog is cancelled, gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.3 exits (code 60, per source) before creating the output file. `start_screenrecording` has no `else` after `if kill -0 $pid`, so it returns 0 and `start_screenrecording || cleanup_webcam` never cleans up.

```text
base default:  cancel in Omarchy region picker -> before overlay and gsr -> nothing left behind
head default:  overlay started -> gsr portal dialog cancelled -> gsr exits
               -> no else branch -> exit 0, no notification, overlay window still open
```

A stubbed sandbox run (no real portal, recorder or camera) matched this for the head default and `--fullscreen` paths: exit 0, no recording file, overlay process still alive. The same path already existed on base with `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_USE_PORTAL=true` (except `--fullscreen`, which stayed on KMS there). This PR makes it part of the default flow.

**Impact:** with `--with-webcam`, a routine cancel leaves the pinned webcam window open with the camera in use. `--stop-recording` does not remove it, because nothing is recording. It stays until the user closes it, starts another webcam recording, or stops a later recording.

**Suggested change:** the open PR #7189 adds a failure branch (notification plus `return 1`, so `cleanup_webcam` runs) and merges cleanly with this PR. It does not tell a deliberate cancel (exit 60) apart from a failure, so combined with this PR every cancelled dialog would show "Screen recording failed to start". Handling exit 60 quietly, while still cleaning up, would fit the new default.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned head `a1004b28`, compared with the earlier head `8a07b82e`, the base and the current `quattro` tip `3faafba2`; omarchy-pkgs at `a701a8db`; pacman 7.1.0, gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.3 and xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland 1.4.1 source. Sandboxed runs: `bin-style-test.sh` and `gsr-kms-caps-test.sh` at the earlier head, and those plus `config-test.sh` at the head, the head merged with `quattro` and a test mutant; a stubbed `command -v`/`omarchy-cmd-present` equivalence matrix; and a stubbed portal-cancel run of the recorder script. The earlier recorder-argument matrix and `/etc` mask case were not rerun, because that code is unchanged. No real `pacman` transaction, capability change, `pkexec` prompt, portal session, camera or btop hardware reading was exercised.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
